items.title: How a Driver’s Sudden Death Triggered Ebola Panic in Congo
items.summary: When a truck driver unexpectedly collapsed and died in a remote village, frontline medical staff scrambled to safely isolate his body, triggering a standoff.

items.title: Europe Unites to Pressure Israel, Breaking With U.S.
items.summary: Britain once followed in France’s slipstream when it came to pressuring Israel. Under new leadership, it is spearheading opposition to Israeli settlements, risking American anger.

items.title: Iran Signals Readiness to Escalate War With U.S. Amid Rising Economic Pressure
items.summary: The Iranian government is taking an increasingly aggressive approach as it confronts a growing economic threat and worries that its grip on the Strait of Hormuz is slipping, analysts say.

items.title: Ukraine’s Unexpected $27 Billion Budget Gap Rattles Europe
items.summary: An unexpected request from President Volodymyr Zelensky offered a stark reminder that the cost of the war will rise, challenging Europe.

items.title: This Tiny Anti-Establishment Party May Put Germany’s Far Right in Power
items.summary: Germany’s far right won a state election but fell short of a majority. Its path to power depends on a small populist group that defies traditional labels.

items.title: The Theme Park at the Heart of France’s Culture War
items.summary: The Puy du Fou is one of France’s most visited theme parks. Its founder says it gives the French a “founding narrative,” but critics say it peddles “far-right propaganda.”

items.title: Israel’s Election Campaign Is Heating Up. Here’s Who’s Running.
items.summary: The contest is shaping up to be a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. It is considered the most consequential in Israel’s history.

items.title: Nepal’s Flood Relief Workers Feel the Pain of Trump’s Cuts to U.S.A.I.D.
items.summary: The agency played an important role in responding to earlier disasters like the 2015 earthquake. But the U.S. and other countries have pulled back, Nepali officials and humanitarian groups say.

items.title: In England — Yes, England — Tea and Cantaloupe Grow as the Climate Warms
items.summary: As British farmers confront intense heat waves tied to climate change, some are cultivating new crops rarely grown in their country.

items.title: Why This Small Dutch Town Is Teaching ‘Adolescence’ in School
items.summary: The Netflix series is seen as a way to kindle debate about gender roles and to confront online bullying.

items.title: Measuring the Cost of Trump’s Multiple Wars
items.summary: Voters and some Republican lawmakers are growing weary of President Trump’s trade battles and the economic fallout from fighting in the Middle East.

items.title: Clay, an A.I. Sales Tool Provider, Raises $115 Million
items.summary: The round was led by Wellington Management, a firm known for investing in start-ups on the path toward potential initial public offerings.

items.title: A.I. Music Giant Suno Tries to Play Nice With Record Labels
items.summary: Suno has drawn copyright lawsuits from the majors. Now it is releasing a version of its A.I. music generator trained in partnership with Warner Music.

items.title: California, an Environmental Bastion, Warms to Nuclear Energy
items.summary: The state is considering extending the life of its last nuclear power plant, Diablo Canyon, and allowing construction of new reactors to help meet its clean energy goals.

items.title: As He Backs ICE Crackdown, Nebraska Governor Employs Undocumented Workers
items.summary: Gov. Jim Pillen’s family business is one of the nation’s largest pork producers. As he seeks re-election, he has aligned himself with President Trump’s anti-immigrant agenda even though his farms have taken on undocumented laborers.

items.title: Oil Hits $100 a Barrel as Turmoil Intensifies in Middle East
items.summary: The cost of crude has risen 40 percent since the start of the war in Iran, pushing up the price of gasoline, diesel and other refined fuels.

items.title: Politics News Site NOTUS Rebrands as The Washington Sun
items.summary: A trademark dispute scuttled its plans to relaunch as The Washington Star, so the site chose a different name.

items.title: TSA PreCheck Now Unlocks Access to Visit Airports Without a Plane Ticket
items.summary: At more than a dozen U.S. airports, T.S.A. PreCheck members can now apply to enter the secure area, even if they’re just going to meet someone on a flight.

items.title: Trump Media Launches MAGA-Friendly Truth Social ETFs
items.summary: The seven exchange-traded funds, like the God Bless America fund, are investing in companies aligned with President Trump’s worldview.

items.title: Carney Says Retaliation Against U.S. Tariffs Was Unavoidable
items.summary: In a video address, the prime minister said the United States was seeking “dependency, not a true economic partnership” from Canada.

items.title: OpenAI Says It Has Cracked One of Math’s ‘Millennium Problems’
items.summary: The company’s announcement is the most dramatic sign yet that artificial intelligence is fundamentally transforming the field of higher mathematics.

items.title: Meta Introduces Muse, an A.I. Agent That Can Send Your Emails and Book Your Travel
items.summary: Muse, Meta’s new A.I. agent, acts as a personal digital assistant that connects to Facebook and Instagram, as well as third-party apps such as Spotify and OpenTable.

items.title: Apple Expected to Unveil a Folding iPhone at Annual Launch Event
items.summary: Fans of the company’s products widely believe it will unveil a folding smartphone at its annual launch event on Wednesday.

items.title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
items.summary: Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.

items.title: How Amazon’s Zoox Is Taking On Waymo in San Francisco
items.summary: The Amazon-owned driverless car company is a distant second to Waymo. Its pitch to riders? Wine pop-ups, festival sponsorships and a car built to be filmed.

items.title: A Hacking Tool Built With A.I. Can Breach Phones Without a Click
items.summary: An attack discovered by A.I. researchers could have compromised hundreds of millions of devices within hours, experts said.

items.title: Key App Developers Have Yet to Embrace Apple’s New Siri A.I.
items.summary: For the company’s new artificial intelligence system to take off, it will need plenty of support from the makers of popular apps on Apple’s phones.

items.title: Virtual Taekwondo Takes the Contact Out of a Combat Sport
items.summary: The contactless version of the Korean martial art is making its debut at this year’s Asian Games. Critics say it’s a glorified video game.

items.title: Early Data Indicates an A.I.-Generated Drug Could Slow Aging
items.summary: Artificial intelligence was used to help develop a drug candidate, rentosertib, for a rare lung condition. Its maker says the drug also seems to reduce the biological hallmarks of age.
